findings.reason: The protected implementation is a compact, cycle-safe graph clone expressed over the three labeled node fields. The copies identity map, explicit stack, original/copied pairing, and shared field loop make allocation and edge translation easy to explain while avoiding duplicated pointer code. The explicit Node and NodeCopy equivalents satisfy the standalone app contract, and no material improvement warrants an inert candidate.

The identity map creates exactly one new NodeCopy for each reachable original and records it before scheduling that original's outgoing edges. For every left, right, and random field, null remains null and a non-null target becomes the unique mapped copy of that target. Early recording makes self-pointers and arbitrary random cycles safe, while every assigned non-null pointer refers only to a copied object. The returned mapped root therefore preserves all values and labeled relationships without sharing node identity with the input.

Each of N original nodes is allocated, scheduled, and processed at most once, and each visit examines exactly three fields, giving O(N) time. The identity map, work stack, and required cloned nodes use O(N) space, matching the declared bounds. The complexity artifact is inherited, hash-bound identity only; this accelerated review did not inspect or recalibrate it and did not claim a fresh runtime verdict.

The implementation handles an empty root, preserves duplicate values by using object identity rather than value keys, translates all child and random targets to NodeCopy objects, and supports null, self, cross-subtree, backward, and cyclic random edges. The returned object uses the required clone class and never aliases an original node.

The complete Approach accurately reframes random pointers as graph edges, explains memoized allocation before exploration, wires all three fields uniformly, and proves deep-copy independence. Its O(N) time and space claims match the protected code and manifest, and its alternatives and edge cases cover two-pass traversal, recursive memoization, missing maps, value matching, serialization-only checks, empty input, null and self pointers, cycles, cross-subtree edges, duplicate values, and sparse trees.

The protected app source and immutable native source remain unchanged at canonical SHA-256 values e5a1ae7f0272306213b9d0a7d44ffcfeb0d8282121799584b7885490501e6289 and 9d31a8e0f1d8737f995362b00a90dd395214bd00782f1cfe214a10c67613200a. Both use the same map, stack, field order, allocation timing, edge assignments, and returned root; their structural differences are limited to the app-local node definitions and native Solution interface. Verified submission 2074761861 remains untouched.

Authenticated Premium evidence confirmed the Node/NodeCopy model, [val, random_index] serialization, deep-copy objective, three exact examples with explanations only for the first two, two constraints, three example diagrams, and two hash-table hints. The modular Reference independently recreates every child and random relationship from all three source images as accessible Mermaid graphs, including null, self, reverse, and cross-subtree targets, without inventing an explanation for Example 3. It is bound to live content SHA-256 4497fbbffb352e37bca25858cd4c630bdfe6f8fa5d1f31426b81b56198f8cdfb.
